newsitem.title: FRANCE: Shell ammonia leak injures 11 in France.
newsitem.headline: Shell ammonia leak injures 11 in France.

text.p: Eleven people were injured, two of them seriously, on Tuesday by an ammonia leak in a refinery owned by Royal Dutch Shell in the southern town of Berre L'Etang near Marseille, refinery officials said.
The incident occurred when about a cubic metre of the toxic chemical leaked out of a small reservoir during routine maintenance at about 8.30 a.m. (0630 GMT), they said.
The leak was quickly sealed off and two workers were taken to hospital by helicopter after suffering serious burns, the officials said.
Nine others suffered only minor injuries and were released after treatment at area clinics.
A Shell spokesman said the accident had not affected refinery operations as the facility had been shut down a week before for regular five-yearly maintenance checks.
The plant is scheduled to resume operating in another four weeks, as expected, the spokesman said.
